Widgets

A cmd widget is a small package: React made of cmd's own elements, reading your agents, terminals and windows live. It draws like a built-in window, asks before it reaches anything, and is tested without a browser.

Make one

cmd widget new my-widget       # a package with a widget, its test, its story, CLAUDE.md
cd my-widget
cmd widget dev                 # on the board, its console here; saves reload it
npm test                       # or cmd widget test
cmd widget check               # package.json, permissions, types
cmd widget preview . --themes all --sizes all

Or ask Magic for one: it writes the same kind of package. Agents working in a package read its CLAUDE.md and this reference, which cmd widget new links at node_modules/@cmd/widget-api/README.md.

cmd · cmd.workspace · cmd.agents · cmd.terminals · cmd.windows · cmd.events · cmd.git · cmd.actions · cmd.stats · cmd.journal · cmd.media · cmd.clipboard · cmd.notify · cmd.net · cmd.ai · cmd.run · cmd.config · cmd.storage · cmd.state · cmd.env · cmd.fmt · Hooks · Frames · Elements · Records

API 1, minor 3. Everything here is in API 1 for good; what came after 1.0 says @since 1.x, and a widget that also runs on an older cmd checks cmd.env.has(name) first (a verb or an element).

cmd

cmd, as a widget sees it. Reads run at once within the widget's grant; acts (1.1) ask the person (docs/55), only right after they pressed something in the widget, and only in its own workspace. Every method is async and rejects with an ApiCallError when the grant lacks what it needs (error.permission names it) or the person says no (code: "denied").

cmd.run

Programs, through the core: cmd.run("gh", ["run", "list"]). Needs run: [<program>].

cmd.storage

JSON values kept by cmd across reloads, restarts and updates, in three scopes: window (this window, 256 KB; the same data as cmd.state), workspace (this package in the window's workspace, shared by its windows there, 10 MB) and package (this package in every window and workspace, 10 MB). Each value is at most 1 MB, each key 1 to 200 characters. A package sees only its own; uninstalling it deletes its data, an update keeps it, deleting a workspace deletes that workspace's. Needs no permission. Live: the hook useStorage(scope, key, initial).

VerbSincePermissionWhat

Each place keeps its own version: the package's data, each workspace's, each window's. When a window starts, each of its places that is behind runs it once, in order package, workspace, window, with scope naming the store to reshape (only it can be written; a place with no data starts at the new version, no migration). If it throws, that place keeps its data and version (places migrated before it stay migrated) and the window says why.

Hooks

The reads as subscriptions: each gets the current value at once and every change after, until its component unmounts.

HookSinceWhat

Needs events: [<class>] for each class of events it reads. { scope: "all" } reads every workspace's, with workspace: ["all"] (live since cmd of 2026-10-15; an older cmd refuses it, and cmd.events.query reads them).

defineWidget<Config extends ConfigShape<Config> = Record<string, WireValue>>(render: (props: { config: Config; }) => ReactNode) => Widget: Declares a widget: render is its view, called with this window's config (live). The module's default export is what cmd runs; a plain component works too. export default defineWidget<{ repo: string }>(({ config }) => <Text>{config.repo}</Text>);

Frames

A frame widget's page ("surface": "frame", its view.html) has a cmd of its own, typed by @cmd/widget-api/frame (/// <reference types="@cmd/widget-api/frame" />): every verb above, by the same name and with the same permissions, limits and asks; no hooks. A verb that needs a press (an act, windows.open) works right after a click in the frame, once per click. The page has no network of its own: its data comes through cmd.

MemberWhat
cmd.<workspace | agents | terminals | windows | events | git | actions | storage | terminalUsage>.subscribe(query?, fn, onError?): () => voidCalls fn with the topic's value now and again on each change (for events: the query's result, then each batch of new events); returns a function that stops it. When the widget restarts it goes on, starting again with the value then. A refusal (the grant doesn't reach it) or its end (the widget stopped) goes to onError, else the console.
cmd.storage.window.subscribe(key: string, fn: (value: WireValue) => void, onError?: (e: FrameCallError) => void): () => voidCalls fn with the key's value now and on each change, from any window of the package (null: none); returns what stops it.
cmd.storage.workspace.subscribe(key: string, fn: (value: WireValue) => void, onError?: (e: FrameCallError) => void): () => voidCalls fn with the key's value now and on each change, from any window of the package (null: none); returns what stops it.
cmd.storage.package.subscribe(key: string, fn: (value: WireValue) => void, onError?: (e: FrameCallError) => void): () => voidCalls fn with the key's value now and on each change, from any window of the package (null: none); returns what stops it.

cmd.on(type: "data", fn: (value: WireValue) => void): () => voidfn when the window's "state", "config" or "theme" changes, a Frame's "data", or on each change of a live topic ("agents", "events" with query…, as cmd.<topic>.subscribe); returns what stops it.
cmd.on<T>(type: T, fn: (value: TopicValue<T>) => void, query?: TopicQuery<T>): () => voidfn when the window's "state", "config" or "theme" changes, a Frame's "data", or on each change of a live topic ("agents", "events" with query…, as cmd.<topic>.subscribe); returns what stops it.
cmd.open(target: string): Promise<{ id: string; }>Opens a URL, a path or a widget in a window beside this one: cmd.windows.open. Only right after a click in the frame.
cmd.ApiCallError: new (e: ApiError) => FrameCallErrorThe class of a refused call's error.

Elements

The app draws each with its kit; a tree can name nothing else. Handlers (onClick, a menu entry's run) are functions in the widget and ids on the wire.

Window

The widget's window, around everything: the title bar (icon and name from the manifest), its status line and menus. Optional; a widget without one gets the bare title bar.

PropTypeWhat
statusstring | nullThe title bar's status line ("2 waiting for you · 1 working"); null for none.
menuMenuEntry[]The title menu (a scope switch: This Workspace / All Workspaces).
actionsMenuEntry[]Entries added to the window's context menu.
childrenReactNodeThe window's content: a View.

View

A window's content frame: toolbar, scrolling body, and the states that replace it.

PropTypeWhat
insetbooleanPads the body by the window inset.
scrollbooleanThe body scrolls (default true).
stateViewState | nullShown instead of the body: empty, loading, no results, error.
childrenReactNodeThe body; a WindowToolbar among them becomes the view's toolbar, a StatusLine its footer.

WindowToolbar

A view's toolbar: buttons, fields, segmented controls. Items that don't fit move to a ⋯ menu.

PropTypeWhat
labelstringIts accessible name ("Filter agents").
bottombooleanUnder the content instead of over it.
childrenReactNodeIts items: ToolbarButton, ToolbarField, ToolbarSearchField, ToolbarSegmented, ToolbarMenu, ToolbarText, ToolbarSpacer.

ToolbarButton

A toolbar button.

PropTypeWhat
label (required)stringThe tooltip and accessible name; shown beside the icon with showLabel.
iconstringAn SF Symbol name; without one it is a text button.
showLabelbooleanShows the label beside the icon while there is room.
pressedbooleanOn (a toggle).
disabledbooleanGreyed out, not pressable.
tone"accent" | "danger" | "needs"A tone for its icon (a count of failures, a change).
badgestring | numberA count after the label.
tipstringA tooltip other than the label.
onClick() => voidPressed.
prioritynumberMoves to the ⋯ menu when there is no room, lowest first; without one it stays.
secondarybooleanFaded until the window is hovered or selected.

ToolbarField

A text field in a toolbar.

PropTypeWhat
value (required)stringThe text in it.
placeholderstringShown while it is empty; also its accessible name.
iconstringAn SF Symbol name before the text.
onChange(value: string) => voidThe text as typed (debounced by the app, which keeps the caret).
onSubmit(value: string) => voidReturn pressed, with the text.
prioritynumberMoves to the ⋯ menu when there is no room, lowest first; without one it stays.
secondarybooleanFaded until the window is hovered or selected.

ToolbarSearchField

A filter field: a magnifying glass, a count, a clear button.

PropTypeWhat
value (required)stringThe filter text.
placeholderstringShown while it is empty ("Filter agents").
countstring | numberWhat matched ("3 of 12").
onChange(value: string) => voidThe text as typed (debounced by the app); "" when cleared.
prioritynumberMoves to the ⋯ menu when there is no room, lowest first; without one it stays.
secondarybooleanFaded until the window is hovered or selected.

ToolbarSegmented

A choice of a few, side by side (a popup when narrow).

PropTypeWhat
value (required)TThe chosen option's value.
options (required){ value: T; label: string; icon?: string }[]The options, in order: a value, a label, an optional SF Symbol.
label (required)stringIts accessible name.
onChange(value: T) => voidAn option was chosen.
prioritynumberMoves to the ⋯ menu when there is no room, lowest first; without one it stays.
secondarybooleanFaded until the window is hovered or selected.

ToolbarMenu

A toolbar button that opens a menu.

PropTypeWhat
label (required)stringThe tooltip and accessible name.
iconstringAn SF Symbol name.
menu (required)MenuEntry[]The menu it opens.

prioritynumberMoves to the ⋯ menu when there is no room, lowest first; without one it stays.
secondarybooleanFaded until the window is hovered or selected.

ToolbarText

A little text in a toolbar (a count, a path).

PropTypeWhat
childrenReactNodeThe text.
prioritynumberMoves to the ⋯ menu when there is no room, lowest first; without one it stays.

ToolbarSpacer

Pushes what follows to the toolbar's end.

No props.

Stack

Children in a column, gap apart.

PropTypeWhat

growbooleanTakes the room left.

Inline

Children in a row, gap apart.

PropTypeWhat

childrenReactNodeWhat it lines up.

Tiles

A grid of equal tiles (stats, cards).

PropTypeWhat

Hide

Drops what doesn't fit the window's size class.

PropTypeWhat

above"narrow" | "regular"Hidden while it is wider.

List

Rows and sections; virtualised by the app, keyed rows keep their place.

PropTypeWhat

ListSection

A heading and its rows.

PropTypeWhat

A row.

PropTypeWhat

A row's icon, or its status light.

PropTypeWhat

A row's text.

PropTypeWhat

ListRowEnd

A row's right end: a chip, an age, a badge.

PropTypeWhat

A small pill of text (an age, a branch).

PropTypeWhat

A number with its label.

PropTypeWhat

Sparkline

A small line of recent values.

PropTypeWhat

Text

Words.

PropTypeWhat

Badge

A label in a tone ("failed", "3 new").

PropTypeWhat

StatusDot

A small status light.

PropTypeWhat

size"sm" | "md""sm" or "md".

Button

A button.

PropTypeWhat

EmptyState

What a view shows when it has nothing: what's missing and how to get some.

PropTypeWhat

Callout

PropTypeWhat

Progress

A progress bar.

PropTypeWhat

Panes

A dashboard's sections: one column, two side by side once the window is wide. Since 1.2.

Pane

PropTypeWhat

Panel

A frame for a list that runs to the window's edges: a WindowToolbar over a PanelBody. Since 1.2.

PanelBody

ListGroup

ListRowActions

Buttons a row shows while the pointer is over it (Run, Stop), in place of its end. Pressing one doesn't press the row. Since 1.2.

CodeBlock

Icon

An SF Symbol on its own (in a line of text, a status line). Since 1.2.

Mark

An icon that gives way to a status light when there is one: a row's, or one in a line of text. Since 1.2.

A change against the period before: ▲ 18% in green when up is good, red when it isn't, dim when flat. Since 1.2.

Something is happening, in a row or a status line. A view that is loading says so with its state instead. Since 1.2.

A view's footer: one quiet line under the content (counts, where it runs). In a View it sits at the bottom edge. Since 1.2.

PropTypeWhat

A button that is an icon alone (a row's Run, a bar's Refresh). Since 1.2.

LinkButton

TextField

A text field in the body (a form, a length to type). The app keeps the caret and sends what is typed, debounced; a filter belongs in the toolbar (ToolbarSearchField). Since 1.2.

PropTypeWhat

Lines over time buckets, filled under when there's one; the period before dashed. For rates, gauges and running totals. Since 1.2.

TimeBars

Bars over time buckets: the current one in the accent, the period before as ticks, an average line. The chart most stats want. Since 1.2.

PropTypeWhat

fillbooleanAs tall as its pane, instead of height.

TimeBar

A track's position (a song's, a video's): played in the accent, moving on by itself while playing. Click or drag to seek. Since 1.2.

Frame

Pixels of the widget's own inside its window: a page of the package (an .html file) drawn in a sandboxed frame, for a canvas, a chart or a player the elements don't draw. The page's cmd is the widget's (@cmd/widget-api/frame), its data comes from data and its messages go to onMessage. Several may share a window. Where pixels aren't drawn (a preview, the phone) its label stands in. Since 1.2.

PropTypeWhat
src (required)stringThe page: an .html file of the package, relative to its folder ("chart.html", "pages/meter.html").
label (required)stringWhat it shows, in words: its accessible name, and what stands in for it where pixels aren't drawn.
heightnumberIts height in pixels; without one it fills the space it is given.
dataWireValue | nullData for the page, as plain values (256 KB at most): cmd.data there, and cmd.on("data", fn) on each change.
onMessage(value: WireValue) => voidThe page sent a value (cmd.post(value)). Not a press: it can't start an act.
